title: Deliver, observe use and measure impact
promise: Complete a verifiable project milestone and keep evidence that another person can inspect.
why: A working demo is only the start. The handoff requires evidence about data, permissions, failure recovery and usefulness in the actual task.

theory.title: Prepare the handoff package
theory.text: Collect setup README, architecture, demo, tests, limits, costs and runbook. Use example credentials and verify that no secrets are included.
theory.example: A package linked from My project that a new person can open and understand.

theory.title: Observe a consented pilot
theory.text: With permission for the data and services, observe one person completing a real task. Record steps, time, errors and assistance. Keep the manual fallback available.
theory.example: Dated observation of one complete task; without permission, keep it pending and use a fictional case.

theory.title: Compare before and after
theory.text: Measure comparable manual and assisted tasks. Include review, repair and cost. Enter values, period and sample size in My project Impact.
theory.example: Net savings with a data source; estimates are not presented as measured savings.

theory.title: Defend and agree maintenance
theory.text: Explain the problem, decisions, introduced failure, repair and outcome to the user. Record owner, a review date in 7 or 30 days, and whether to keep, improve or retire it.
theory.example: Confirmed owner and recovery procedure; the academy date is a record, not a scheduled notification.

errors.fix: Run the case and save the observation; leave it pending if blocked.

canDo: Help draft test cases and explain observed errors
cantDo: Certify tests that nobody ran or approve on behalf of another person
words: A record of what actually happened, tied to a version and a test.
